interest: For economic and diplomatic historians of interwar Japan and the Great Depression, this file highlights the critical role and financial fragility of the Japanese sericulture sector, which tied millions of agrarian households directly to American textile markets. The cross-references point to key archival records detailing the seasonal credit dependency of silk filatures purchasing cocoons from farmers and direct Japanese government interventions, specifically the controversial liquidation of raw silk stocks to American silk magnate Paolino Gerli in 1932.
overview: This file consists of two State Department cross-reference sheets (document file notes) from April and June 1932 categorized under decimal subject 894.6225 (Japan: Silk Culture). The sheets index diplomatic communications from Edwin L. Neville, U.S. Chargé d'Affaires ad interim in Tokyo, cross-referencing Telegram No. 107 (filed under 894.50/59) and Despatch No. 634 (filed under 894.00-P.R./54). Together, they highlight the economic conditions of the Japanese sericulture industry during the Great Depression, noting the agricultural financing required by filatures to purchase seasonal cocoon crops from farmers and the commercial complications arising from the Japanese Government's direct sale of silk stocks to American silk merchant Paolino Gerli.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a telegram regarding the agricultural nature of the silk industry and the financing of cocoon purchases by filatures.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Section D of Telegram No. 107 sent on April 6, 1932, by Edwin L. Neville from Japan to the State Department, originally filed under 894.50/59. The note summarizes that the silk industry remains primarily agricultural in character and highlights that filatures buying cocoons from farmers depend on recurring bank loans to finance their purchases. It points researchers to broader documentation on Japan's financial and economic conditions during the spring 1932 cocoon season.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Telegram No. 107 from Neville on silk industry financing

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing a report on the Japanese Government's sale of silk to Paolino Gerli and resultant industry complications.
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Despatch No. 634 (filed under political report series 894.00-P.R./54), dated June 1, 1932, from Edwin L. Neville in Japan to the Department of State. It records the Japanese Government's transaction disposing of silk reserves to prominent American silk dealer Paolino Gerli. The note records that this state-negotiated sale created severe disruptions and commercial complications across the silk industry.
subfiles.title: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 634 from Neville on government silk sale to Paolino Gerli
